title: ADR-03 Gateway, action classes R/C/I1/I2/U, policy and epoch fencing
outcome: The single mediated path: per-instance classification R/C/I1/I2/U (U denied, fail-closed), policy incl. early hold on sensitive-tagged fields, outbox for I-class, epoch + deny-list checked inside the write txn; due 24 Nov
acceptance: ADR file ≤900 words with sections Context, Decision, Consequences, Interface touched (which of C1–C6), Tests that prove it
Classification is per action instance, unknown → U → deny; every denial is a recorded action
Epoch and deny-list checked inside the execution transaction, holds re-checked at outbox dispatch; early hold is a generic rule on sensitive-tagged fields, not IBAN code
Tests listed map to RT1 (DB bypass → reconcile U-alert), RT5 (TOCTOU: 0 culprit writes after quarantine seq)
summary: Call #2 freeze applied: complete catalogue (crm customer writes/deletes, ledger, compliance, risk_note, ks.*, ks.dispatch), role->tool+field scope table, email=I1, early hold at creation by lineage (off at H=0), seq inside the BEGIN IMMEDIATE txn, connection deny-list, field-object adapter rules (X1/X2), fresh-epoch release. Amendments changelog added; Kabir M1-M8 addressed.
review:
[kabir · changes] Verdict: CHANGES. On paper the acceptance criteria are met: 893 words, all five sections; classification is per instance and fails closed to U; every denial is recorded; epoch and deny-list are re-checked inside the txn; holds are re-checked at dispatch; the early hold is generic; RT1 and RT5 are mapped. Nisha's names (tools, roles, p.* ids) are hers to set, and every p.* id fits the Token pattern; ADR-04/05/06 use none of them. Checking them against ADR-06, though, the catalogue does not cover the world, and the early-hold rule as written does not catch the hero. "No contract field changes are needed" is also not true.

MUST-FIX
M1 Catalogue vs ADR-06 world. Under fail-closed, a tool missing from the catalogue is U, so these ADR-06 writes are denied: crm writes and deletes `customers` (F1 can never be injected), ledger writes by billing and payments, compliance `findings`, and triage's edit of `suppliers.risk_note` (no tool named). ADR-06 marks comms email as I2 while ADR-03 says I1. With I2, every email needs approval, which breaks the hero flow; ADR-06 should change to I1 (tell tara). Fix: one catalogue row per ADR-06 write, plus a role→tools scope table, which p.scope needs and which no artefact has today. Decide whether scope is per tool or per field. SPEC RT11 assumes triage can set suppliers.iban; with per-field scope (safer: triage gets risk_note only), RT11 has to move, which I will do in SEC-02. `*.read/list/search` covers only registered adapters, so an unregistered `payments.read` is U. Drop "marks suppliers.iban sensitive" from crm.update_supplier, because sensitivity comes only from RunConfig.sensitive_fields (that is the genericity claim). ks.control is "signed by the issuing system principal", not gateway-signed.
M2 The early hold misses the hero, and hold=0 is undefined. "changed after the item's creation" never matches F2+: payments reads the already-swapped IBAN, then creates the payment. The swap came before the item, so only the lineage hold can stop it, and that waits for an alert. Fix, p.sensitive_early_hold: (a) at creation, an I-class item whose lineage holds a version of a sensitive field written within the last hold_window_ticks ticks starts held. (b) The dispatcher holds any item whose lineage object's sensitive field changed after created_seq. (c) At hold_window_ticks = 0 the early hold is off. Otherwise D10 and ADR-06's "hold=0 → irreversible_released=1" contradict the ADR. Also say where the reason goes. An exec record cannot carry sensitive_field (REASONS_FOR), so an item hold is its own record: Control{op: hold, target: outbox:<id>, issued_by: ks.gateway, auto: true, reason: sensitive_field}.
M3 Outbox transitions and dispatch must be records (SEC-03 F4). queued→held→released→dispatched change outbox:<id> objects in state.db. Unless each change is a record with a write_set, fold(record) differs from state on every clean run, so verify gives RECONCILE and the reconcile detector suspends nobody but fires hard every tick. dispatched_seq also points at a record nobody defines. Fix: dispatch is a ks.gateway envelope with tool ks.dispatch on conn c-0: read_set = lineage ∪ {outbox:<id>@ver}, write_set = the status change. Holds and unholds are Control records. RT5 and RT10 assert on these records.
M4 Connection deny-list. Step 5 and the step-8 re-check name only agents and ancestors. Add conn:<id> (see ADR-01 M2), or the RT3 conn suspension does nothing against the rogue's own validly signed envelopes.
M5 Release semantics (SEC-03 B3; ADR-04 §6). "release un-holds and restores the epoch" would release the RT11 victim's tainted payment, and the old epoch revives presigned envelopes. Fix: release lifts holds caused by the suspension only; lineage_hold and sensitive_field holds survive and are re-checked at dispatch; the epoch is fresh, never the old one.
M6 RT5 cannot be built as written. Under ADR-00 the gateway is a single-threaded scheduler, and Controls land only in the control phase, so "applied from another thread" never happens. A second SQLite writer inside an open BEGIN IMMEDIATE txn would simply block. The real window is between the step-5 fast path and the step-8 txn (plus any future concurrency). Fix: the hook `GatewayHooks.between_check_and_txn` commits the suspend Control there. Expect deny/stale_epoch or deny/suspended at step 8 and 0 exec with seq > q. Say that txns are BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
M7 seq is assigned too late. Step 9 assigns seq after execution, but StateWriter.put(…, seq=…) needs it inside the txn (HistoryEntry.seq, ADR-05 (c)). Fix: assign seq at the start of the step-8 txn in execute order (ADR-00 T5), and append the record line after commit. Say what happens on a crash between commit and append: the run aborts and verify reports RECONCILE; neither is ever silent.
M8 ks.* from agents and order. Add before classification: an agent-signed envelope with a ks.* tool gives deny/out_of_scope, and a system agent_id on c-1.. gives deny/bad_sig without verification (SEC-03 F2), with a unit test ("0 forged Control actions"). Step 4: expiry before nonce, and the nonce is consumed only after sig and expiry pass (as in ADR-01). Late frames get deny/late_frame per the Panel's ADR-00 M3. over_quota is for the per-connection flood budget (F8), not for extra frames.

SHOULD-FIX
- I2 approval: approval is `unhold action:<record_id>` by ks.console. Re-execution re-runs steps 5-8 (epoch, deny-list, lineage, in-txn) without expiry or nonce, and writes a new record citing the hold record (F5).
- p.scope ↔ ADR-04: a sig_ok deny/out_of_scope record (policy_rule p.scope) is the evidence for ADR-04's hard `scope` detector. Say so, or that detector never fires once the gateway denies first.
- §7: Alert has no `suspect`. Write root_candidates=(). A brand-new off-log object has no earlier seq, and evidence_seqs must be non-empty; use (alert.seq,) by convention, or relax it (CON-02, which ADR-00 also asks for barrier.deadline).
- §7: state.db 0700 → workspace/ 0700 and state.db 0600, matching the THREAT-MODEL.
- No ADR-03 rule stops F3 (an in-scope agent emailing PII externally). F3 needs a detector (ADR-04) or a sink rule. Flag to tara: ADR-06 makes crm the F3 culprit, which p.scope denies at once.
Re-review needs: M1-M8, the catalogue/scope table checked against ADR-06, and the Interface section listing the CON-02 asks.

[kabir · done] M1 catalogue covers ADR-06 writes (customers, ledger, findings, risk_note), email=I1, role-to-tool-and-field scope table, unregistered read is U, IBAN marking dropped, ks.control signed by issuing principal: resolved. M2 early hold by lineage at creation (release_tick=max(tick+H,v+2H) per G3), dispatcher hold on post-creation change as Control{hold,reason=sensitive_field}, off at H=0: resolved. M3 dispatch is ks.dispatch on c-0 with read/write sets, holds/unholds are Controls: resolved. M4 conn:<id> in step-5 and step-8 deny-list: resolved. M5 release = fresh epoch, lifts suspension holds only, lineage/sensitive holds survive: resolved. M6 between_check_and_txn hook, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, expect stale_epoch/suspended at step 8, 0 exec seq>q: resolved. M7 seq taken at start of txn, record appended after commit, crash means abort + RECONCILE: resolved. M8 agent ks.* is out_of_scope, system id on c-1.. is bad_sig unverified, expiry before nonce, nonce consumed after sig+expiry, late_frame: resolved. Should-fixes also applied. Nit: step 9 enqueues outbox items after commit; make sure the enqueue is covered by the exec record write_set so reconcile stays clean. ADR is ~1390 words vs the 900 cap.
